<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>D</c>écimo octávo Kaléndas Maii Luna octáva. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>S</h>olémnitas sancti Ioseph, Sponsi beátæ Maríæ Vírginis, Confessóris et universális Ecclésiæ Patróni.
<h>S</h>ancti Iustíni, Philósophi et Mártyris, cuius memória prídie huius diéi recensétur.
<h>R</h>omæ, via Appia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Tibúrtii, Valeriáni et Máximi, sub Alexándro Imperatóre et Almáchio Præfécto. Horum duo primi, beátæ Cæcíliæ exhortatióne ad Christum convérsi et a sancto Urbáno Papa baptizáti, póstmodum, ob fídei confessiónem, fústibus cæsi, gládio percússi sunt; Máximus vero, Præfécti cubiculárius, cum et ipse, eórum permótus constántia et angélica visióne firmátus, in Christum credidísset, támdiu plumbátis verberátus est, donec spíritum exhaláret.
<h>I</h>nterámnæ sancti Próculi, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
<h>E</h>ódem die sancti Ardaliónis mimi, qui, dum Sacris Christianórum in theátro illudéret, derepénte mutátus est, et ea non solum verbis, sed étiam testimónio sui sánguinis comprobávit.
<h>I</h>nterámnæ sanctæ Domnínæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, cum Sóciis Virgínibus coronátæ.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sanctæ Thomáidis Mártyris, quæ a sócero, cuius impudícis nolúerat consentíre votis, gládio percússa est atque in duas partes per médium discíssa.
<h>L</h>ugdúni, in Gállia, sancti Lambérti, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>A</h>lexandríæ sancti Frontónis Abbátis, cuius vita sanctitáte et miráculis cláruit.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Abúndii, Mansionárii Ecclésiæ sancti Petri.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.573c18b41b:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>pril 14th 2027, the 8th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>he Solemnity of St. Joseph, spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary, confessor, and patron of the Universal church.
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy martyr Justin, the admirable philosopher. He had presented to the Emperors Marcus Antoninus Verus and Lucius Aurelius born Modus his second book in defence of our religion, and was then earnestly spreading the same at Rome by his disputations when he was accused of Christianity through the devices of Crescens the Cynic, whose life and infamous manners he had rebuked, and for a reward of his faithful speaking he received upon this day the crown of martyrdom.
<h>U</h>pon the same 14th day of April, were born into the better life:
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, upon the Appian Way, under the Emperor Alexander and the Prefect Almachius, the holy martyrs Tiburtius, Valerian, and Maximus. Tiburtius and Valerian had been converted to Christ by the exhortations of blessed Cicely and baptized by the holy Pope Urban, and for the confession of their faith were cudgelled and beheaded. Maximus was a chamberlain of the Prefect, and was moved to believe in Christ by beholding the steadfastness of Tiburtius and Valerian, and being confirmed in the same faith by an apparition of angels, he was lashed to death with scourges loaded with lead.
<h>A</h>t Terni, the holy martyr Proculus, Bishop of that see, [about the year 306.]
<h>O</h>n the same day, the holy martyr Ardalion. He was a player, and was making a mock upon the stage of the sacred rites of the Christians, when he was converted all of a sudden, and attested his conversion not only by his words but also by his blood, [about the year 300.]
<h>A</h>t Terni, the holy Virgins and martyrs Domnina and her Companions, [about the year 272.]
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, [in the fifth century,] the holy martyr Thomais.
<h>A</h>t Lyon, the holy Confessor Lambert, Bishop of that see, [in the year 688.]
<h>A</h>t Alexandria, the holy Abbot Fronto [—in the desert of Nitria, he had 70 monks—] famous for the holiness of his life, and for his miracles, [in the reign of Antonine, about the year 151.]
<h>A</h>t Rome, [in the sixth century,] holy Abundius, watchman of the Church of St. Peter.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
